title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Grothendieck defines, for k-additive categories B', B with a tensor product and associativity, unit and commutativity constraints, a 'multiplicative structure' on a k-additive functor F: B' -> B. It consists of morphisms u_{X,Y}: F(X)⊗F(Y) -> F(X⊗Y) and a unit map α: 1_B -> F(1_{B'}), compatible with the three constraints. In modern terms this is a lax symmetric monoidal functor.

This page draws the consequences.
(1) NB: 1_{B'} is a commutative monoid in B', so F(1_{B'}) is a commutative unital monoid object ('objet-anneau') of B. It is a k-algebra when everything is k-linear.
(2) More generally, F carries commutative (unital, associative) monoids of B' to monoids of the same kind in B. This is the standard fact that lax monoidal functors preserve monoids.
(3) Such F, with suitable morphisms, form a category. They compose, B'' -> B' -> B. This gives a 2-category of k-additive ⊗-categories, lax ⊗-functors and ⊗-natural transformations.
(4) Specialisation: take B' = K. K is a (k-linearised) category of finite semi-simplicial sets, or a variant. A k-linear functor F: K -> B is then identified with an object C of B^·. Here C is a semi-(co)simplicial object, i.e. the cochain-complex-type datum indexed by the standard simplices, from which F is recovered by additivity/linearity.
(5) Definition by transport: a 'multiplicative structure on the cochain complex C^·' is a lax symmetric monoidal structure on the corresponding functor K -> B. Grothendieck proposes the name 's.h. mult. demi-simpliciale' to avoid confusion with strict dg-algebra structures.

The next page makes this explicit. The data reduce to maps F(Δ^i)⊗F(Δ^j) -> F(Δ^i * Δ^j) for standard simplices. Dualising gives maps (C^i⊗C^j)⊗(chains of the product/join of simplices)^∨ -> C, i.e. an Eilenberg–Zilber / Alexander–Whitney-type system of higher cup products packaged functorially.

The problem served: giving an intrinsic, coherent notion of 'multiplicative structure' (homotopy-commutative cup-product structure) on the ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes studied in the dévissage project, e.g. cochains with coefficients in B. It is encoded as lax monoidal functors out of a combinatorial model category of simplices rather than as a strict dg-algebra.
errors: Possible inconsistency with the previous page. There α: 1_B -> F(1_{B'}) appears to be called an 'isom.'. If α is an isomorphism, the NB that F(1_{B'}) 'becomes' a ring object is trivial, since it is just the unit 1_B. The NB is only meaningful for lax (non-unital-strong) functors, which is the modern convention.

The monoidal structure on K is left unclear. Finite semi-simplicial sets have a categorical product whose realisation is not the product of realisations. The next page writes both × and * (join), so which tensor structure on K is intended (product via Eilenberg–Zilber, or join) is not fixed. The identification 'F ⇔ C ∈ B^·' also tacitly needs F to be determined by its values on standard simplices (e.g. via additivity/finite colimit preservation), which is not stated on this page.

Variance is not specified. Cochains are contravariant in simplicial sets, and the next page dualises (C^∨). So either K is meant as an opposite category, or F is a chain-type functor whose dual gives the cochain complex.

ideas.what: Lax (symmetric) monoidal functor between k-additive symmetric monoidal categories: maps F(X)⊗F(Y)->F(X⊗Y), 1->F(1), compatible with associativity, unit and commutativity constraints
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bénabou (1963-67); Eilenberg–Kelly (1966); Saavedra Rivano (1972, ⊗-foncteurs, Grothendieck school)
ideas.where_published: Closely related to Saavedra's thesis (Catégories tannakiennes), written under Grothendieck's direction; not sure of a Grothendieck-authored text

ideas.what: A lax monoidal functor sends the unit to a commutative monoid and sends (commutative) monoids to (commutative) monoids

Defining a multiplicative ('s.h.') structure on a semi-simplicial cochain complex C in B as a lax monoidal structure on the k-linear functor K -> B (K = linearised finite semi-simplicial sets) that C determines
ideas.modern_name: algebra structures as lax monoidal functors out of a model category of simplices / Day-convolution monoids; cf. monoidal Dold–Kan, E∞-structures on cochains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Day (1970) for convolution; Schwede–Shipley (2003) monoidal Dold–Kan; Hinich–Schechtman (1987), Mandell (2001), Berger–Fresse (2004) for E∞ cochains

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes encoding multiplicative (cup-product, homotopy-commutative) structures on semi-simplicial cochain complexes in an arbitrary k-linear ⊗-category B as lax symmetric monoidal functors from a linearised category of finite semi-simplicial sets into B, under the name 's.h. mult. demi-simpliciale'. This is a functorial 'theory-style' alternative to operadic E∞/strong-homotopy definitions. It is not developed in any published Grothendieck text known to me.
missed.quote: Un foncteur k-lin. K —F→ B s'identifie donc à un C ∈ B^·. Donc en ce sens ce qu'il faut entendre par "structures multiplicatives sur le complexe de cochaînes C^·" de B^· (on dira : s.h. mult. demi-simpliciale" pour ne pas prêter à confusion).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early (c.1975) instance of the idea that cochain-level commutativity data should be modelled as monoidal functors from a combinatorial category of simplices, with values in a general tensor category, not only in modules. It is mildly of historical interest as a precursor to Day-convolution / monoidal Dold–Kan and E∞-cochain formalisms. The general idea is now standard, so it is not new mathematically.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly a routine unpacking of lax monoidal functors. The only notable point is the proposal to define homotopy-multiplicative structures on semi-simplicial cochain complexes in a general ⊗-category as lax monoidal functors out of linearised finite semi-simplicial sets. That is a historically interesting precursor, but the idea is well covered by later literature.
transcription_corrections: 'objet-[-(?)-] anneau': the crossed-out part is likely a false start; read 'objet-anneau'.
'(catégorie des ensembles ½ simpliciaux finis, ou ses variantes, genre ...)': plausible reading. The trailing text after 'genre' is illegible scribble.
's.h. mult. demi-simpliciale': 's.h.' may abbreviate 'structure homotopique(ment)' or Stasheff's 'strongly homotopy'. The reading is uncertain; possibly 'str. mult.'.
'B^·' (C ∈ B^·) is probably the category of semi-(co)simplicial complexes in B, not B itself; the superscript dot is visible.
